correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=4 and all unordered distinct non-cycle chord pairs and nonnegative fractions x, the base-cycle slow eigenvalue is isolated of multiplicity two. Exact orthonormal cosine/sine Fourier projection gives each squared chord length as (8/n)sin²(pi d/n) and projected angle via endpoint sums. The smaller eigenvalue of a convex combination of two projected rank-one matrices has an exactly optimized rational expression. The odd, divisible-four, and two-mod-four cases exhaust all available lengths/angles; the strict inequality s(2-s-s²)/(2(2-s²))>0 eliminates every nonorthogonal competitor in the last class. A positive fixed-n spectral separation yields a uniform O_n(epsilon²) remainder. The executable check enumerated 707078 finite chord pairs for n=4..32 and directly diagonalized selected full Laplacians, but the theorem relies on the analytical proof, not the finite census.

value.rationale: A repeated slow mode makes all single-edge additions ineffective for cycle convergence, so the smallest useful shortcut budget is exactly two links. The theorem solves the natural pairwise placement-and-weight design for every cycle order and identifies the non-obvious n≡2 mod4 regime where a near-diameter link beats a second diameter and receives more conductance. This supplies an exact structural and quantitative small-budget consensus-rate rule beyond a routine generic spectral inequality; no paper-sized downstream theorem is claimed.
